```{r}

library(ggplot2)
data(msleep)

plot(msleep$sleep_total,msleep$bodywt)

plot(msleep$sleep_total~msleep$bodywt)

```

```{r}
plot(msleep$sleep_total~msleep$bodywt, pch = 16, col="blue", bty="L")

plot(msleep$sleep_total~msleep$bodywt, pch = 16, col="blue", bty="L", xlab="Bodyweight (grams)", ylab= "Total Sleep (hours)") 

```
```{r}
plot(msleep$sleep_total~msleep$bodywt, pch = 16, col="blue", bty="L", xlab="Bodyweight (grams)", ylab= "Total Sleep (hours)")

abline(lm(msleep$sleep_total~msleep$bodywt))
```

```{r}

msleep$colors=NA

msleep$colors[msleep$sleep_total >= 17] <-"red"
msleep$colors[msleep$sleep_total < 17] <-"black"


plot(msleep$sleep_total~msleep$bodywt, pch = 16, col=msleep$colors, bty="L", xlab="Bodyweight (grams)", ylab= "Total Sleep (hours)") 

```

```{r}
hist(msleep$sleep_total, col=rainbow(10))

plot(msleep$sleep_total~as.factor(msleep$order), col=rainbow(19)) 

plot(msleep$sleep_total~msleep$bodywt, pch = 16, col=msleep$colors, bty="L", xlab="Bodyweight (grams)", ylab= "Total Sleep (hours)") 

boxplot(msleep$sleep_total~as.factor(msleep$order), col=rainbow(19)) 

plot(msleep$sleep_total~as.factor(msleep$vore),col=rainbow(4), xlab="Bodyweight (grams)", ylab= "Total Sleep (hours)")
```
# Exercise 1: Practicing Base R Plotting
# Name: Nicolas Galgano
# Date: 11/7/2026

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)

# Load the msleep dataset
data(msleep)
```


# ============================================================================
# Task 1: Create and customize a scatterplot
# ============================================================================
# Create a scatterplot of sleep_total vs bodywt (body weight).
# Customize your plot with:
# - A point character (pch) of your choice
# - Blue colored points
# - Axis labels: "Body Weight (kg)" for x-axis and "Total Sleep (hours)" for y-axis
# - A border style of your choice (bty)

# Your code here:
```{r}
plot(msleep$sleep_total~msleep$bodywt, pch = 14, col="Blue", bty="U", xlab="Body Weight (kg)", ylab= "Total Sleep (hours)") 
```



# ============================================================================
# Task 2: Make a histogram
# ============================================================================
# Create a histogram of the brainwt (brain weight) variable.
# Customize your histogram with:
# - A color of your choice (col)
# - An appropriate x-axis label
# - A descriptive title using the main argument

# Your code here:
```{r}
hist(msleep$brainwt, col="purple", xlab = "Brain Weight (kg)", main = "Distribution of Brain Weight Across Species")

```



# ============================================================================
# Task 3: Create a boxplot comparing groups
# ============================================================================
# Create a boxplot showing sleep_total for each vore type (diet).
# Customize your boxplot with:
# - Different colors for each box (hint: use rainbow() or choose specific colors)
# - Appropriate axis labels
# - Convert vore to a factor using as.factor()

# Your code here:

```{r}
boxplot(msleep$sleep_total~as.factor(msleep$vore), col=rainbow(4), xlab = "Diet", ylab = "Sleep Total (Hours)", main = "Total Sleep by Diet")
```


# ============================================================================
# Bonus Challenge (Optional)
# ============================================================================
# Create a scatterplot of any two continuous variables from msleep.
# Add a line of best fit using abline() and lm().
# Color points based on a condition you define (like we did with sleep_total >= 17
# in the tutorial), and add a legend to explain the colors.

# Your code here:

```{r}
msleep$colors[msleep$bodywt >= 10] <-"red"
msleep$colors[msleep$bodywt < 10] <-"green"
plot(msleep$bodywt, msleep$sleep_total, col = msleep$colors, xlab = "Body Weight (kg)", ylab = "Total Sleep (Hours)")

# Line of best fit
abline(lm(msleep$sleep_total ~ msleep$bodywt))

# Legend
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Body weight >= 10 kg", "Body weight < 10 kg"),
       col = c("red", "green"),
       pch = 19)
```


# Plotting with ggplot tutorial
```{r}
data(state)
states = as.data.frame(state.x77) # convert data to a familiar format - data frame
str(states) # let's take a look at the dataframe

ggplot(data=states) 

ggplot(data=states, aes(x=Population, y=Income))+geom_point() 

ggplot(data=states, aes(x=Population, y=Income))+geom_point()+geom_smooth(method="lm") 

```





```{r}
ggplot(data=states, aes(x=Population, y=Income))+geom_point()+geom_smooth(method="lm")+theme_minimal() 
ggplot(data=states, aes(x=Income, y=Illiteracy, color=Population)) +geom_point()+geom_smooth(method="lm", color="red")+theme_classic() 

```


```{r}
ggplot(msleep, aes(y=sleep_total, x=sleep_rem, group=as.factor(vore), color=as.factor(vore))) +geom_point()

```



```{r}
ggplot(msleep, aes(y=sleep_total, x=sleep_rem, group=as.factor(vore), color=as.factor(vore)))+
  geom_point()+
  labs(y= "Total Sleep (hours)", x= "REM sleep (hours)")+
  theme_minimal()+
  scale_color_manual(name="Diet", 
                        labels = c("Carnivore", 
                                   "Herbivore", 
                                   "Insectivore", 
                                   "Omnivore", 
                                    "NA"), 
                        values = c("carni"="blue", 
                                   "herbi"="red", 
                                   "insecti"="green", 
                                   "omni"="brown", 
                                   "NA"="orange"))
```

```{r}
g<-ggplot(msleep, aes(y=sleep_total, x=sleep_rem, group=as.factor(vore), color=as.factor(vore)))+
  geom_point()+
  labs(y= "Total Sleep (hours)", x= "REM sleep (hours)")+
  theme_minimal()+
  scale_color_manual(name="Diet", 
                        labels = c("Carnivore", 
                                   "Herbivore", 
                                   "Insectivore", 
                                   "Omnivore", 
                                    "NA"), 
                        values = c("carni"="blue", 
                                   "herbi"="red", 
                                   "insecti"="green", 
                                   "omni"="brown", 
                                   "NA"="orange"))
g
```

```{r}
ggplot(iris, aes(y=Sepal.Length, x=Sepal.Width, group=Species, color=Species))+
  geom_point()+
  facet_wrap(~Species)+
  geom_smooth(method="lm")
```

```{r}
ggplot(ChickWeight, aes(x=Time, y=weight, group=Diet, color=Diet))+
  stat_summary(fun=mean, geom="point", size=1)+
  stat_summary(fun=mean, geom="line", size=1)+
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", 
               aes(width=0.1), size=0.5)
```
# Exercise 2: Practicing ggplot2

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)

# Load the msleep dataset
data(msleep)
```



# ============================================================================
# Question 1: Basic scatterplot with the msleep dataset
# ============================================================================
# Create a scatterplot showing the relationship between bodywt (body weight) 
# and brainwt (brain weight). Add appropriate axis labels and change the 
# theme to theme_classic().

# Your code here:
```{r}
ggplot(data=msleep, aes(x = bodywt, y = brainwt)) +
    geom_point() +
    labs(x = "Body Weight (kg)",
       y = "Brain Weight (kg)",
       title = "Body Weight vs. Brain Weight")+ 
  theme_classic()
```



# ============================================================================
# Question 2: Adding color by group
# ============================================================================
# Using the same variables from question 1 (bodywt and brainwt), color the 
# points by vore (diet type). Make sure to convert vore to a factor.
# Add a legend title that says "Diet Type".

# Your code here:
```{r}
ggplot(data=msleep, aes(x = bodywt, y = brainwt, color=as.factor(vore))) +
    geom_point() +
    labs(x = "Body Weight (kg)",
       y = "Brain Weight (kg)",
       title = "Body Weight vs. Brain Weight",
       color = "Diet Type")+ 
  theme_classic()
```


# ============================================================================
# Question 3: Scatterplot with a line of best fit
# ============================================================================
# Plot sleep_total against sleep_cycle. Add a linear regression line using 
# geom_smooth(). Color the line red and use theme_minimal().

# Your code here:
```{r}
ggplot(data = msleep, aes(x= sleep_total, y = sleep_cycle, color = "red")) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth() +
    labs(x = "Sleep Cycle Length (hours)",
       y = "Total Sleep (hours per day)",
       title = "Total Sleep vs. Sleep Cycle Length")+
  theme_minimal()
```


# ============================================================================
# Question 4: Faceted plots by group
# ============================================================================
# Create a scatterplot of sleep_total vs sleep_rem. Use facet_wrap() to 
# create separate panels for each vore type. Add appropriate axis labels.

# Your code here:
```{r}
ggplot(data= msleep, aes(x = sleep_total, y = sleep_rem)) +
  geom_point()+
  facet_wrap(~vore)+
  labs(x = "Sleep Total (hours)",
      y = "Rem Sleep (hours)",
      title = "Total Sleep vs. Rem Sleep by Diet")
```


# ============================================================================
# Question 5: Exploring a new dataset
# ============================================================================
# Load the built-in iris dataset. Create a scatterplot showing Petal.Length 
# vs Petal.Width. Color points by Species. Add a title to your plot using 
# ggtitle("Iris Petal Dimensions"). Choose your favorite theme.

# Load the iris dataset
data(iris)

# Your code here:
```{r}
ggplot(data = iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, y = Petal.Width, col = Species)) +
  geom_point()+
  ggtitle("Iris Petal Dimensions") +
  theme_dark()

```


# ============================================================================
# Bonus Challenge (Optional)
# ============================================================================
# Pick any two continuous variables from the msleep dataset and create a 
# publication-quality plot with:
# - Appropriate axis labels
# - A theme of your choice
# - Points colored by a grouping variable
# - A descriptive title

# Your code here:

```{r}
ggplot(data = msleep, aes(x = awake, y= bodywt, col = vore)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()+
    labs(x = "Hours Awake",
      y = "Body Weight (kg)",
      title = "Hours awake vs. Body Weight") +
  theme_classic()
```
